draft.title: Adding and subtracting integers
card: Integers are whole numbers, including negatives and zero. On a number line, numbers to the right are greater. So \(-2\) is greater than \(-7\).
Adding a positive number moves right. Adding a negative number moves left. For example, \(3 + (-5)\) starts at 3 and moves 5 left, to \(-2\).
Subtracting a positive number moves left. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive. For example, \(4 - (-3) = 4 + 3 = 7\).
Worked example: \(-6 - (-2) = -6 + 2 = -4\). Start at \(-6\) and move 2 right.
draft.remember: Taking away a negative gives the same result as adding a positive.

a.why: Subtracting \(-4\) is the same as adding 4, so \(5 + 4 = 9\). The answer \(1\) comes from treating the problem as \(5 - 4\) and ignoring the negative sign.
a.clue: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

b.q: At 5 am the temperature in Ballarat was \(-3\) degrees. By noon it had risen 11 degrees, then at night it fell 9 degrees. What was the night temperature in degrees?
b.why: Rising 11 gives \(-3 + 11 = 8\). Falling 9 gives \(8 - 9 = -1\). The answer \(1\) comes from dropping the negative sign at the end.
b.clue: Do the rise first, then the fall, moving along the number line.
